title: Locally finite regular CW complex with cellular G-action
body_html:
Locally finite regular CW complex with cellular $G$-action

The standing geometric setup is the following data.

  • $X$ is a locally finite regular CW complex. Regular means the attaching map from the boundary of each cell to $X$ is an embedding. Locally finite means every cell is contained in the closure of finitely many cells.
  • $G$ is a (locally profinite) group acting continuously and cellularly on $X$: $G$ permutes the set of cells and the action restricted to each cell is a homeomorphism.
  • $R$ is a coefficient ring.

The underlying topological space of $X$ is denoted $|X|$. We write $[\![X]\!]$ for the set of cells of $X$, and $[\![X]\!]_d$ for the $d$-dimensional cells. The face relation $E \preceq F$ holds when $E \subseteq \overline{F}$.

Two further standing notations:

  • $\Fix_G(S) := \{g \in G : g \cdot s = s \text{ for all } s \in S\}$ — pointwise stabilizer.
  • $\Stab_G(S) := \{g \in G : g \cdot S = S\}$ — setwise stabilizer.

For a cell $E$, $\Fix_G(E)$ and $\Stab_G(E)$ may differ; refining the CW structure can force them to agree.

Lean formalisation

The topological setup distils to a purely combinatorial poset-with-dimension abstraction. Poset structure, dimension, local finiteness, and cellular $G$-action are separate typeclass layers stacked on the same carrier type — each a class / structure in its own right:

Ingredient Kind Lean signature KB node
face poset + dimension data-carrying class class AbstractCellComplex (X) [PartialOrder X] (with field dim : X → ℕ) Abstract cell complex
local finiteness Prop-valued class class IsLocallyFinite (X) [PartialOrder X] : Prop Locally finite abstract cell complex
$G$-action compatibility Prop-valued class class GCellComplex (G) [Group G] (X) [PartialOrder X] [AbstractCellComplex X] [MulAction G X] : Prop Cellular G-action on an abstract cell complex
face-closed subsets structure structure Subcomplex (X) [PartialOrder X] (with a separate SetLike instance) Subcomplex of an abstract cell complex
topology on the face poset scoped instance : TopologicalSpace X (Alexandrov star topology) Alexandrov star topology on the face poset

None of these classes extends its underlying [PartialOrder X] / [MulAction G X] / [AbstractCellComplex X]: those are taken as separate instance parameters, so the cell-poset data, the group action, and the compatibility conditions can be stacked, refined, or replaced independently.

The "locally finite regular CW complex with cellular $G$-action" is realised by the standing variable block

variable {G : Type*} [Group G]
variable {X : Type*}
variable [PartialOrder X] [AbstractCellComplex X] [IsLocallyFinite X]
variable [MulAction G X] [GCellComplex G X]

Every downstream Lean definition — cosheaves, chain complex, equivariant functors, induction, QFD — is stated against exactly this typeclass stack. Regularity of the CW complex is not tracked as a Prop mixin at the abstract level; it re-enters only in the geometric-realisation direction, where it identifies a fixator of the open cell with a fixator of its closure.

Two distinct subgroups are attached to a cell $E$, and both are needed:

  • $\Stab_G(E) = \mathrm{MulAction.stabilizer\ G\ E}$ — "$g$ maps $E$ to itself";
  • $\Fix_G(E) = \bigcap_{F \preceq E} \Stab_G(F)$ — "$g$ fixes $E$ and every one of its faces".

These are genuinely different at the poset level (they agree only on minimal cells). The abstract induction / QFD machinery in the Lean library is stated using the setwise version $\Stab_G(E)$; the pointwise version is available when a specific geometric input supplies a down-monotone cell fixator. See Cellular G-action on an abstract cell complex for the definitions and the design rationale.

lean_refs.name: SheafOnBuilding.AbstractCellComplex
lean_refs.signature:
class AbstractCellComplex (X : Type*) [PartialOrder X] where
  /-- Dimension function. -/
  dim : X → ℕ
  /-- Strict monotonicity: a proper face has strictly smaller dimension. -/
  dim_lt : ∀ {E F : X}, E ≤ F → E ≠ F → dim E < dim F
  /-- Every cell of positive dimension has a face of dimension one
  less.  Without this axiom one could have a "2-cell" attached
  directly to a vertex with no edges in between, which is not the
  face poset of any regular CW complex. -/
  exists_face_dim_pred :
    ∀ {F : X}, 0 < dim F → ∃ E : X, E < F ∧ dim E + 1 = dim F

lean_refs.signature:
class GCellComplex (G : Type*) [Group G] (X : Type*)
    [PartialOrder X] [AbstractCellComplex X] [MulAction G X] : Prop where
  /-- The action preserves the face relation. -/
  smul_le : ∀ (g : G) {E F : X}, E ≤ F → (g • E) ≤ (g • F)
  /-- The action preserves dimension (cells map homeomorphically). -/
  smul_dim : ∀ (g : G) (E : X),
    AbstractCellComplex.dim (g • E) = AbstractCellComplex.dim E

structure Subcomplex (X : Type*) [PartialOrder X] where
  /-- The underlying set of cells. -/
  carrier : Set X
  /-- Closed under taking faces. -/
  face_closed' : ∀ {E F : X}, E ≤ F → F ∈ carrier → E ∈ carrier
